t: I will buy vs I’m going to buy vs I’m buying | WordReference Forums
s: October 11, 2020 - I agree with Barque (the post above) that (1) is more emphatic (shows more intent) than (2). (1) is also more formal than (2). In everyday conversation, (2) would be more commonly heard than (1) unless you wanted to emphasize your intent to buy a computer. (3) is written in the present progressive tense, which, because it shows continuous action extending from the present to some point in the future can substitute for the future tense. (3), in my opinion, is inbetween (1) and (2) in its formality. Not to make things too complicated, but you could also say, "I will be buying a new computer tomorrow."
